name: BZ wave fragments (sub-excitable)
description: Light-sensitive Belousov–Zhabotinsky (Oregonator). Under strong light the medium is sub-excitable: a broken wave neither spreads into a full wave nor dies at once, but travels as a compact wave fragment. Fragment size is held by global feedback, as in Sakurai, Mihaliuk & Showalter's experiments: the light follows the total excitation (phi_e = phi + K_h·mean u), so when fragments grow the light dims them back and when they shrink it lets them grow — a lone fragment settles to a fixed size and keeps it indefinitely. Because the budget is shared, several fragments compete: here the strongest takes over and the others fade (winner-take-all). Colliding fragments annihilate where they overlap (excitation waves can't cross). Things to try: the seed brush makes new fragments (drag a short line); K_h = 0 turns the feedback off (fragments then grow into bands or die); lower phi to ≈0.05 with K_h = 0 for spirals; paint phi high for light barriers; a small kernel_sigma (e.g. 20) makes the feedback local instead of global.
